I'll fix this by masking escapes and code spans together in a single left-to-right pass.

input.description: Test new masking regex in node

content.text: I fixed the bug in `src/` but haven't run anything: the Node check was blocked by a permission prompt, so I worked through the cases by hand. **Cause:** Before it looks for emphasis, the lexer builds a masked copy of the line so that escapes, code spans and links can't be mistaken for `*`/`_` markers. The step that masks backslash escapes (`src/Lexer.ts:400`) ran over the whole line, including inside code spans. So in `` `C:\Users\` `` the final `` \` `` was read as an escaped backtick and hidden. The step that masks code spans then paired the wrong backticks, the opening one of `` `C:\Users\` `` with the opening one of `` `D:\` ``. That treated everything between them, `**home**` included, as code, so it was never turned into ``. **Fix:** - **`src/rules.ts`**: new inline rule `escapeOrCodeSpan`. It scans left to right and matches either a backslash escape, a whole code span (same definition as the inline `code` rule), or a backtick run that doesn't close. - **`src/Lexer.ts`**: the escape-masking step now uses that rule. It masks only the escapes and leaves code spans and stray backtick runs unchanged. Backslashes inside a code span therefore stay literal and can't escape the closing backtick. Escapes outside code spans are masked as before, so `` \`*a*\` `` still treats the backticks as escaped. The existing `anyPunctuation` rule is unchanged, since other code uses it to unescape link URLs, titles and fence info strings. The pedantic, GFM and breaks rule sets all build on the normal set, so they pick up the new rule automatically. Traced by hand, both examples from the report give the expected output: `home` in the first, and `a\ b c` in the second. The test suite still needs running to confirm nothing else changed.
